structure:
A Playwright trace corpus of the Design Release 2.1 prototype (GB-notification-service, served under /design-release-2.1), recorded on 27 November 2026 with Playwright 1.61.1 by the fit-style suite in workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/prototype-specs/e2e (the prototype:dr2-1-specs source). 156 trace zips sit flat in workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/traces-prototype/, with index.json mapping each zip to its spec, test title, status and the pages it walked. All 156 passed. They come from 12 spec files: about-the-consignment (22: notification type, origin of the import, what are you importing, main import reason, germinal section 1), address-book (9: the INS address book list, add, view, edit, delete), consignment-parties (14: the roles and addresses page and its pickers, CPH number, add-address hand-offs, permanent address, contact address), dashboard (9: prototype index, overall dashboard, live animals and germinal products category dashboards, at a glance drill-downs), description-of-the-goods (13: commodity details, total gross weight, identification details per species, additional details), documents (7: upload documents), eudpa-691 (4: Back and return-to-hub behaviour of the run), journeys (9: 5 whole journeys end to end, about 250 actions each, and 4 notification hub tests), manage-notifications (7: view, amend, cancel amend, copy as new, delete), snagging (37: snags S01 to S38, without S30, each a focused look at one page's look and feel), templates (12: manage, create, view, edit, change, use, delete) and transport-and-arrival (13: arrival details, transit countries, transporter details, add a transporter). Most traces walk the opening run (create-notification, notification-type, origin, what are you importing, reason) to reach their page, so those pages recur in nearly every trace. A sample opened with tim's Playwright 1.65.0 showed 40 to 260 actions a trace, about 5 per page walked, and 0 errors; failed-validation states are shown as rendered pages, not trace errors. The corpus is indexed from index.json in trace-prototype-dr2-1.work/index-dr2-1.tsv. The scope is every trace in the folder; it leaves out nothing in it, but it shows only what the suite walked, so pages and branches the suite did not reach (and the prototype's intro, /design-release-2 and /testing areas) are not here. The parts are cut by journey step group across spec files: each snagging section goes with the part that owns its page, the end-to-end journeys are two parts of their own, and dashboards, manage notifications, templates and the address book are a part each.

Extracted in 18 parts:
Part 1, Notification type and origin of the import: Part 1 mined all 13 traces its read names, in full, and read both spec files (about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js and snagging.fit.spec.js). The 13 traces: from about-the-consignment, notification type (3: create new asks what is being imported, starting from a category dashboard skips the type question, plants for planting reaches an empty commodity search), origin of the import (4: renders the origin questions, region code Yes reveal and empty-code error, country optional and answers kept, country search keeps the pick) and germinal section 1 (1: create new on the germinal products dashboard); from snagging, S01 to S05 on the origin page (5), three of which (S02, S03, S04) also open the page in a second browser context with JavaScript off. Every trace is a core-journey or validation trace over the same opening run. Refs below name each trace by its zip file name in sources/traces-prototype/ and an action id from `actions`, or a request id from `requests`. Pages in journey order: (1) /create-notification, a redirect with no page of its own: with no category it sends the user to (2) /notification-type, 'What are you importing?' (caption 'About the consignment'), five radios and a Continue button, shown only when a notification is started with no category; with ?category=live-animals or ?category=germinal-products (the Create new buttons on the /live-animals and /germinal-products dashboards) it skips the type question and goes straight to (3) /origin-of-the-import, 'Origin of the import' (caption 'About the consignment'), always shown: a Draft status strip with the notification type and reference, Country of origin (a search box with suggestions), 'Does the consignment have a region of origin code?' (Yes reveals a code box with the country's two-letter prefix), 'Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)' and one Save and continue button. It continues to /what-are-you-importing, which part 2 owns; this part claims only that the run reaches it, and what plants for planting finds there. Error states rendered: the type question with nothing chosen, and Yes with no region code. No trace recorded an error. The country search runs in the browser: no data call fired while typing.

claims.statement: The trace never follows the delete page's 'No, cancel' link or its Back link, so what cancelling a delete does is not shown.
The trace never uses the list's Type filter, so whether it filters on the client or by submitting the GET form, and what it shows, are not seen.
No trace shows a search that finds nothing, or the empty state of a category with no addresses.
No trace shows the last page of a category (page 3 of Origin and Consignor) or a Previous link being followed.
No trace shows format validation for the postcode, email address or phone number on the add or edit pages: no badly formed value was entered.
No trace shows the find-address errors for a badly formed postcode or a postcode with no addresses, or the select-an-address error for continuing without choosing an address.

No trace saves a Destination, Consignee or Importer address or a Branch address, so the save, the success banner and how those rows show in their list are not seen. The trace also never shows what happens when no use is ticked.
No trace views, edits or deletes a Destination, Consignee and Importer, a Transporter or a Branch entry, so their entry pages, including whether a transporter shows its approval number, are not seen.
No trace presses the edit page's Cancel button, so where it leads is not seen.
No trace uses the select-an-address page's 'Change postcode' or 'Enter address manually' links, so what they keep or clear is not seen.
